text:
incident-bot: P1 alert — inference-high-latency for customer 'Acme Corp'. 95th latency > 5s across eu-west-1. Paging primary oncall now.

sara: oncall ack. I'm booting into the dashboard and tracing requests. assigning dave as secondary for the handoff if I need to step out.

dave: ack. I'll stand by. can you paste the SLO dashboard link?

sara: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/inference/latency?range=15m — 95th spiked from ~250ms to ~5.2s at 02:12 UTC. Error rate is low.

jin (runtime-oncall): noting: KV cache hit ratio dropped ~80%->40% right around spike. Could be cache eviction or model change. I'll tail runtime logs.

incident-bot: Automated snapshot: scaled_replicas=8 -> 8, gpu_utilization=72%, queue_depth increased from 3->18.

sara: trying quick mitigation: increasing runtime pool by +2 nodes and forcing prefix cache warmup for hot routes. Doing a gradual scale so we don't OOM infra.

```bash
# actions taken
kubectl scale deploy runtime-pool -n inference --replicas=10
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/admin/cache/flush?scope=prefixes
```

tori (infra-oncall): I see transient OOMs on node inference-n3 at 02:13 UTC, automatic pod restarts happened. I'll check the node GPU driver logs and node-level memory pressure.

lia (support-oncall): looping in CS for Acme. Sending them an interim note: "We are investigating latency spikes; mitigation in progress. Will update in 15m." Do we want to open an incident bridge for them?

sara: yes please open bridge. Lia, share the bridge link and timeline. Also adding runbook pointer: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/inference-high-latency. Follow section "fast mitigations" first.

jin (runtime-oncall): quick note: model rollout 1.4 was promoted to canary at 01:50 UTC. Canary traffic is routed to 1.4 and looks like it altered KV cache keys (new tokenizer chunking). If canary expanded, that would explain cache misses.

dave: who owns canary promotion? product OR runtime? We need to know if promotion was manual.

sara: runtime triggers canary via CI -> deploy pipeline. Jin, can you confirm if 1.4 was auto-promoted?

jin (runtime-oncall): checking deploy pipeline logs... looks like pipeline auto-promoted after 10% canary stability metric hit at 01:59 UTC. Promotion to stable occurred at 02:05 UTC. I can roll back canary if we suspect it.

tori (infra-oncall): infra note: node affinity for the new pods put some replicas on older driver nodes (n3) which have a slight memory leak vs the newer n5 nodes. That combined with increased memory per model could cause OOM churn.

sec-bot: security alert check — no anomalous auth events in the window. Request patterns are typical. No immediate security signal.

lia (support-oncall): CS confirmed bridge is open and Acme is on it. They've asked about root cause and ETA. We should give them a safe ETA (~30m) until stable metrics return.

sara: propose immediate mitigation: roll back model to v1.3 on stable, scale +2 runtime nodes, and re-run cache warmup. If that reduces latency, we'll keep rollback and schedule a controlled canary with the new tokenizer change in staging. Thoughts?

jin (runtime-oncall): rolling back now to v1.3 on stable traffic. I'll keep 10% canary with 1.4 disabled from auto-promotion.

```bash
# rollback
kubectl set image deploy/inference-stable inference-model=registry/redwood/model:v1.3
# pause canary auto-promotion
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/pipeline/canary/pause?pipeline=inference-canary
```

incident-bot: Mitigation action logged by sara and jin.

sara: observing metrics after rollback: 95th dropped to ~320ms within 3 minutes. Queue depth returning to normal. Good signal.

lia (support-oncall): relaying to Acme: "Latency appears to have normalized after rollback; we're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a postmortem."

dave: excellent. I'll take the next steps for handoff — I'm primary for next shift from 04:00->10:00 UTC. Sara, any coverage gaps we should flag?

sara: FYI — we currently have no designated secondary between 06:00-08:00 UTC due to PTO. Tori, can infra cover escalation during that window if things get weird?

tori (infra-oncall): I can be on-call overlap 06:00-07:00 UTC to cover immediate escalations, but not the whole window. Recommend adding an on-call backup or swapping PTO. Ops team, please advise.

lia (support-oncall): CS notes: Acme wants a timeline for the permanent fix. We'll coordinate on a follow-up once postmortem is ready.

jin (runtime-oncall): action items I have: 1) disable auto-promo until tokenizer change reviewed 2) create deterministic cache migration script 3) add a guard to canary that checks KV key shape before promotion. I'll open tasks in infra/runtimes backlog.

sara: security asks: sec-bot reported no anomalies but let's add an audit check around the promotion pipeline to confirm no unexpected artifacts. Jin, can you tag sec in the pipeline PR?

sara: for the handoff: I'm leaving notes in the incident bridge and the runbook. dave, you're primary now. If infra needs help escalate to tori, runtime to jin, security to sec-bot (or sec oncall). Support/CS is lia.

incident-bot: Severity downgraded to P2 at 02:22 UTC — latencies stable.

dave: thanks team. I'll own the postmortem and schedule the follow-up with CS. Also will annotate the runbook with the tokenizer/canary checklist to prevent auto-promo surprises.

sara: great handoff. I'm leaving the bridge and marking my shift handoff in the oncall calendar. dave, ping me if you need anything.

tori (infra-oncall): I'll follow up on node driver patching and recommend a patch window.

sec-bot: I'll run a deeper audit overnight and attach findings to the postmortem.

lia (support-oncall): I'll file a CS follow-up and copy the postmortem link once available.

sara: final note for runbook updates: add a section "canary tokenization change risk" + explicit check for KV key compatibility and an ops gate for auto-promotion.

dave: noted. closing thread for now, will reopen if metrics regress.

incident-bot: Thread closed by dave at 02:33 UTC."
